messages:
alice: Heads-up — customer `acme-retail` on dedicated pool rp-uk-02 is seeing a sudden throughput drop (~60%) and elevated p99 token latency starting ~02:00 UTC. They report intermittent 429s and a lot of tiny batches. I have a repro trace and minimal steps below.

ben: saw the alert. any indicators it's a noisy-tenant vs scheduler regression?

carla: SRE bot posted a throttle spike 02:03 UTC for rp-uk-02: `dedicated_throttle_rate > 0.25` and queue depth oscillation. attaching perf counters soon.

alice: quick repro steps I used on staging (very small):
```bash
# single request flood reproducer
for i in {1..200}; do \
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
    -d '{"model":"gpt-large-8k","input":"short prompt","max_tokens":32}' &
done
```
Observed runtime logs showing continuous-batcher draining into windows of size 1-2 frequently.

ben: can you paste the batcher debug snippet?

alice: logs (trimmed):
```
batcher: enqueue req id=0x7f2 size_tokens=20 timestamp=1610000023
batcher: window_open quantum=8 remaining_capacity=8
batcher: scheduled pack size=1 reason=deadline
batcher: dispatch batch_size=1 tokens=22
kvcache: miss tenant=acme-retail key=...
```

carla: that "reason=deadline" suggests continuous-batcher fallback hitting micro-deadlines instead of packing. Might be quantum mis-estimation after kernel changes.

david: we rolled kernel scheduling change last week (sched-quantum tweak). Could be regression. Any correlation with deployments around 02:00?

sre-bot: [ALERT] rp-uk-02: batch_dispatch_rate drop 62% | avg_batch_tokens down 0.4 -> 0.9 | throttle_rate up 0.18 -> 0.42

eva: I checked release history — a perf tweak to prefill/kv cache eviction landed in canary at 01:50 UTC. Might increase miss-rate and push more small requests through.

ben: immediate mitigation suggestions: 1) increase min_batch_tokens for acme-retail tenant to 16, 2) temporarily pin tenant to a higher priority queue to avoid noisy neighbors, 3) revert the sched-quantum change in canary.

alice: tried 1) locally — bumping min_batch_tokens to 16 reduces tiny dispatches but raises p50 slightly. Need a customer-safe plan.

carla: also check max_batch_tokens config — if we have aggressive max token cap per microwindow, packer may split requests early.

david: action plan:
- carla to confirm if sched-quantum change is causal (bisect)
- eva to roll a targeted revert on canary and monitor rp-uk-02
- ben to apply tenant-level min_batch_tokens=16 and enable sticky priority for acme-retail
- alice to collect a 10m flamegraph and KV miss-rate snapshot

alice: flamegraph link: https://perf.internal/graphs/3123456789 (will upload traces). KV miss-rate jumped 4x at 02:00.

carla: small note — if eviction policy changed, KV misses can prevent prefix caching which increases per-request token decode and prevents packing.

ben: also saw auth-layer retries in the logs causing repeated tiny requests. check client-side retry backoff.

alice: customer said they didn't change client code. but we found some 500->retry loops in our proxy at 02:01.

david: rolling a revert on the prefill eviction tweak to canary now. watching metrics.

sre-bot: [INFO] canary rollback started at 02:18 UTC for prefill-eviction-change

eva: monitoring dashboard: avg_batch_tokens for rp-uk-02 climbing back to baseline after revert — p99 latency dropping.

alice: customer confirmed errors decreased, throughput recovering to ~85% after tenant-level changes + rollback.

ben: follow-ups — we should add an automated alert for avg_batch_tokens < 2 and a runbook step to check prefill/kv miss-rate + sched-quantum diffs.

carla: agree. also add a metric for "deadline-caused dispatches" so we can distinguish deadline vs packing-induced sends.

alice: I'll file a postmortem stubbing the timeline and RCA with the actions above. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
